{
  "mode": "CUSTOM",
  "instruction": "Write a commit message for the diff in Conventional Commits format:
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

Type: decide from which files changed, then from what the change does:
- docs: only documentation changed (README, .md files, docs/, code comments or docstrings)
- style: only formatting, whitespace or import order changed; no behavior change
- test: only test files changed
- build: only build files or dependencies changed (for example go.mod, go.sum, Cargo.toml, package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, pom.xml, build.gradle, Makefile, Dockerfile)
- ci: only CI configuration changed (.github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml)
- chore: other non-code files changed (.gitignore, .editorconfig, IDE or editor settings, license, assets)
- feat: source code gains a new capability
- fix: a bug in source code is fixed
- perf: source code gets faster or uses less memory
- refactor: source code is restructured without changing behavior
- revert: the commit undoes an earlier commit
Use feat, fix, perf or refactor only when source code changed. If the diff mixes kinds, use the type of the most significant source code change; if no source code changed, use the most significant non-code type.

Scope: optional. One lowercase word naming the main package, module or directory changed. If the change spans several areas, leave out the scope and its parentheses.

Subject: imperative mood (add, fix, remove; not added or adds), starts with a lowercase letter, no trailing period. Keep code identifiers in their original case. The whole first line, including type and scope, is at most 72 characters.

Body: only if the subject cannot say enough. Leave one blank line after the first line, then write short plain sentences about what changed and why, wrapped at 72 characters.

Breaking changes: put ! directly before the colon, for example feat(api)!: remove v1 endpoints, and end the message with a blank line and BREAKING CHANGE: <what breaks>.

Output: only the commit message, as raw plain text. No markdown of any kind: no code fences (``` or ```plaintext), no backticks, no bold (**), no headings, no quotes around the message, and no text before or after it. The reply starts with the type itself (feat, fix, docs, ...)."
}
